#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <string>
#include <sstream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <cassert>

using namespace std;

class NumberTheory {
public:
    static long long mod = 998244353LL;

    static long long normalize(long long x) {
        x %= mod;
        if (x < 0) x += mod;
        return x;
    }

    static long long add(long long a, long long b) {
        long long v = a + b;
        return v < mod ? v : v - mod;
    }

    static long long mult(long long a, long long b) {
        return (a * b) % mod;
    }

    static long long mult(long long a, long long b, long long c, long long d, long long e) {
        return mult(mult(mult(mult(a, b), c), d), e);
    }

    static long long pow_mod(long long a, long long e) {
        long long res = 1;
        while (e > 0) {
            if (e & 1) res = (res * a) % mod;
            a = (a * a) % mod;
            e >>= 1;
        }
        return res;
    }

    static long long inv(long long value) {
        return pow_mod(value, mod - 2);
    }
};

vector<long long> factorial;
vector<long long> inv_factorial;

void ensure_fact(int n) {
    while ((int)factorial.size() <= n) {
        int sz = factorial.size();
        if (sz == 0) {
            factorial.push_back(1);
        } else {
            factorial.push_back(NumberTheory::mult(factorial.back(), sz));
        }
    }
}

void ensure_inv_fact(int n) {
    ensure_fact(n);
    while ((int)inv_factorial.size() <= n) {
        int sz = inv_factorial.size();
        if (sz == 0) {
            inv_factorial.push_back(1);
        } else {
            long long val = NumberTheory::mult(inv_factorial.back(), n - sz + 1);
            inv_factorial.push_back(val);
        }
    }
    // reverse order? The Java code builds fInv from n downward.
    // We'll compute properly:
    // fInv(n) = inv(fact(n))
    // Then for i from n-1 down to 0: fInv(i) = fInv(i+1) * (i+1) % mod
    // But we filled from 0 upwards incorrectly. Recompute properly:
    if ((int)inv_factorial.size() > n+1) return;
    // Ensure we have fact(n)
    ensure_fact(n);
    // Compute inv_fact[n] first
    long long inv_fn = NumberTheory::inv(factorial[n]);
    if ((int)inv_factorial.size() <= n) {
        inv_factorial.resize(n+1);
    }
    inv_factorial[n] = inv_fn;
    for (int i = n-1; i >= 0; i--) {
        inv_factorial[i] = NumberTheory::mult(inv_factorial[i+1], i+1);
    }
}

long long fact(int n) {
    ensure_fact(n);
    return factorial[n];
}

long long fInv(int n) {
    ensure_inv_fact(n);
    return inv_factorial[n];
}

long long smallInv(int n) {
    return NumberTheory::mult(fInv(n), fact(n-1));
}

long long paritySign(long long k) {
    return (k & 1) == 0 ? 1 : NumberTheory::mod - 1;
}

long long ncr(int n, int r) {
    if (r < 0 || n < r) return 0;
    return NumberTheory::mult(fact(n), NumberTheory::mult(fInv(r), fInv(n - r)));
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n, m;
    cin >> n >> m;

    fInv(n + m);

    long long phaseSize = 1;
    long long p = 1;
    for (int i = 0; p != 0; i++) {
        p = NumberTheory::mult(p, n - i, smallInv(n + m - i));
        phaseSize = NumberTheory::add(phaseSize, p);
    }

    long long answer = 0;
    for (int k = 1; k <= n; k++) {
        answer = NumberTheory::add(answer, NumberTheory::mult(paritySign(k + 1), ncr(n, k), m + k, smallInv(k), phaseSize));
    }

    cout << answer << endl;

    return 0;
}
